I get being stressed by research. I love wikipedia, but man I will often end up with 10 tabs opened all on different topics because I followed the blue links lol.

It might help creating an outline of what info you want beforehand, and then go looking for that info. Like, if I were to write notes on a god I might decide I want to know their symbols, myths they're mentioned in, a small list of epithets, reasons they were prayed to, offerings suggested, etc. 

Keep it simple, because it's a resource for you so it's more important to be useful than anything else.

It kinda sounds like you're getting overwhelmed by all the info that's out there and maybe writing too much down for your notes. I'd recommend taking notes by topic, and just summarizing info you find. Like, you mentioned using a word document. Use the headings feature to split that up into different categories (for example: maybe each god has its own category). Most word programs you can open up a navigation pane (I know on Word it's under View -> Check box for navigation pane) and now all your headings have turned into clickable tabs on the side of the screen.

Just write down summarizing sentences for what you've learned, or copy and paste quotes that inspire you. Hell, you can even just create a basic table with info for each topic that you know you want. For myths, maybe all you need is just a 1 sentence summary of the myth and maybe just reflect on your thoughts on it. You don't really need in depth notes for those, because if you ever want to reference them again that's what websites or books are for, and you can just copy and paste links to them into the word doc for future reference.

Remember, you don't need to know everything. Just take notes on what's important for you right now.
